meta.title: Solace — mental health screening for university students
meta.description: A short, anonymous DASS-21 screening for university students, with instant results and clear next steps. You are not alone.

header.quickExitLabel: Quick exit: leave Solace for another site. You can also press Esc twice.
header.langSwitchLabel: ID, switch language to Bahasa Indonesia

footer.disclaimer: Solace is a screening tool, not a diagnosis.
footer.disclaimerDetail: Results do not replace an assessment by a professional. If you are in immediate danger, contact your local emergency services.
footer.independence: No ads and no trackers. Solace is not affiliated with any clinic, hospital, or practice.
footer.quickExitHint: Press Esc twice for a quick exit.

landing.title: It is okay if you do not know yet what you are feeling.
landing.subtitle: A private DASS-21 screening to understand symptoms of depression, anxiety, and stress, with clear next steps.
landing.startHint: Free, can be started without an account, about 5 minutes.
landing.resumeBody: {answered, plural, =0 {You started a screening but haven't answered the first question yet.} one {# of 21 questions is answered and saved on this device.} other {# of 21 questions are answered and saved on this device.}}
landing.lastResultTitle: Your last result is still saved
landing.lastResultBody: Your last screening result is saved on this device.
landing.trustTitle: What to know before you begin

trust.account: You can begin without creating an account.
trust.local: Without an account, answers stay on this device.
trust.screening: Helps recognise symptoms; it does not diagnose.

landing.storyTitle: Sometimes what feels heavy does not have a name yet.
landing.storyBody: Solace gives you room to pause, answer honestly, and see a more structured picture—without putting a label on who you are.
landing.privacyNoAccountBody: You can take the screening and see your results without an account. Your answers stay on this device.
landing.privacyNoEmailBody: If you create an account later, all you need is a username and a passphrase. No email, real name, or student ID.
landing.privacyEncryptedBody: If you use an account, your answers and notes are encrypted in your browser before they are saved. Without an account, screening answers stay on this device.
landing.howIntro: Get to know the process before you begin. You can pause and decide what comes next at your own pace.
landing.stepsPreviewSafety: Then, one safety question before your results are shown.

understand.title: Know what will happen before you begin
understand.body: Age confirmation and consent come first. You can read how data is stored and where this tool's limits are before answering anything.

answer.title: Answer one statement at a time
answer.body: There are 21 statements about the past seven days, followed by one separate safety question. There is no timer, and you can return to earlier answers.

choose.title: See a summary, then choose what is useful to you
choose.body: When you finish, you can prepare a report for a psychologist or continue to research-based tips. The decision remains yours.

landing.howResult: Your results appear right away. Then you choose: download a report for a psychologist, or continue to research-based tips.
landing.notDiagnosis: Solace helps you recognise symptoms. It does not give a diagnosis.
landing.resumeExpiry: Your answers are kept on this device and deleted automatically if you don't continue within 7 days.
landing.evidenceTitle: Designed for moments that can feel vulnerable
landing.evidenceBody: Trust does not come from big claims. It is built through clear boundaries, support that comes first, and careful treatment of data.

privacy.title: Privacy follows your choice
privacy.body: Without an account, screening answers are stored on this device. If you use an account, sensitive data is encrypted in the browser before it is stored.

safety.title: Safety always comes first
safety.body: The safety question is separate from your score. If an answer shows an urgent need, Solace presents access to support before anything else.

useful.title: A summary you can bring
useful.body: Results explain three subscales and can be prepared as a PDF to support a conversation with a professional.

landing.resultsBody: Three subscales are shown with categories and context drawn from your answers. Solace then helps make your next options clearer.
landing.resultsNote: Every result has context. A full assessment takes place with a qualified professional.
landing.resultsPreviewFooter: Include the sections you choose, then download a PDF to bring to a consultation.
landing.toolkitTitle: Small supports you can try right away
landing.toolkitBody: These exercises do not replace professional support. Use them as brief companions when you want to slow the pace or notice your surroundings again.
landing.groundingBody: Gently direct your attention to what you can see, touch, hear, smell, and sense.
landing.groundingLabel: Grounding sequence from five to one
landing.groundingPace: Take the time you need. You can choose any step.
landing.faqIntro: Short answers about Solace's purpose, data, and support.

diagnosis.question: Does Solace give a diagnosis?
diagnosis.answer: No. Solace is a self-screening tool that helps you recognise symptoms. A diagnosis can only come from a professional after a full assessment.

account.question: Do I need to create an account?
account.answer: Not to begin the screening or see your result. An account is used if you choose to save history and use the available follow-up features.

privacy.question: How is my privacy protected?
privacy.answer: Without an account, screening answers stay on this device, and an unfinished draft is removed after seven days. Sensitive account data is encrypted in the browser before storage.

support.question: What if I need help now?
support.answer: Use the I need help now button at the top. If your safety answer shows an urgent need, Solace presents the support page before your results.

duration.question: How long does it take?
duration.answer: Usually about five minutes, with no time limit. You answer 21 statements and one separate safety question.

landing.finalKicker: Begin with what is possible today
landing.finalTitle: You do not have to understand everything at once.
landing.finalBody: Take a few minutes to notice what is happening, at a pace you choose for yourself.

simulator.title: Interactive Result Preview
simulator.hint: Select a severity level to see an example of how results are presented:
simulator.contextNormal: Scores sit within the general population range. Maintaining sleep routines and positive habits is encouraged.
simulator.contextMild: Mild symptoms are indicated. Spotting early triggers and practicing relaxation techniques can help.
simulator.contextModerate: Symptoms sit at a moderate level. Talking with a campus counselor or mental health professional is recommended.
simulator.contextSevere: Scores indicate a high emotional burden. Solace prioritises support directories and professional counseling resources.
simulator.contextExtremelySevere: Symptoms sit at an extremely severe level. We recommend talking to a professional; you don't have to face this alone.

scenarios.title: When is Solace typically used?
scenarios.intro: Academic and life burdens often accumulate unnoticed. Screening helps map out what you are experiencing.
scenarios.academicBody: Back-to-back assignments, thesis revisions, and graduation targets causing persistent tension.
scenarios.nightBody: When your body is exhausted but your mind will not stop replaying worst-case scenarios and future worries.
scenarios.burnoutBody: Things that once brought joy begin to feel empty, heavy, and emotionally draining.
scenarios.socialBody: Feeling behind compared to peers, or carrying the burden of always needing to appear fine.

start.title: Before you start
start.intro: There are 21 statements about how you have felt over the past 7 days, then 1 safety question. There are no right or wrong answers, and you can go back to earlier questions at any time.
start.autosave: Your answers are saved automatically on this device, so you can stop and continue later.
start.minorTitle: Solace is designed for people aged 18 and over
start.minorBody: So this screening will not start. If something is weighing on you, try talking to an adult you trust, such as a parent, guardian, or school counsellor.
start.minorHelp: If you feel unsafe, you can contact the services below.
start.consentLabel: I understand that Solace is a screening tool, not a diagnosis, and that my answers are saved on this device.
start.replaceWarning: Starting a new screening will replace the previous result saved on this device.
start.requirements: Choose your age and tick the consent box to start.

screening.instructions: Choose how much this statement applied to you. There are no right or wrong answers.
screening.keyboardHint: Press 1–4 to choose, then Enter to continue.
screening.autosaveHint: Answers are saved on this device.
screening.chooseToContinue: Choose one answer to continue. You can change it before moving on.
screening.answerSelected: Answer selected. You can change it before moving on.
screening.placeholderNotice: The Indonesian question text is not final yet. Placeholder text is shown for now.

safety.title: One more question
safety.intro: This question is separate from the 21 questions and is not part of your score. We ask everyone so we can show the right kind of support.
safety.period: This question covers the last 2 weeks.
safety.withdrawBody: Did you change your answer because you picked the wrong option earlier, or because you felt unsure about sharing? Either way, that's okay. The list of support services stays on your results page.

crisis.title: You are not alone.
crisis.intro: Thank you for being honest. Feelings this heavy can change, and help is available right now. Choose the step that feels most possible for you at the moment.
crisis.privacy: Solace never contacts anyone on your behalf, and no data is sent from this page.
crisis.talkBody: Psychological support services you can reach by phone or chat.
crisis.calmBody: If everything feels too fast, try one of these exercises.
crisis.breathingStatic: Breathe in slowly for 4 seconds, then breathe out for 6 seconds. This guide repeats automatically.
crisis.breathingVibrationHint: Optional. A brief vibration when switching between breathing in and out.
crisis.breathingVibrationUnavailable: Vibration is not available in this browser or on this device.
crisis.groundingIntro: Notice what is around you, one step at a time:
crisis.planBody: A safety plan is a personal note to help you get through hard moments. You can start thinking about it now:
crisis.planWarningSigns: Signs that a hard moment might be coming
crisis.planDistraction: People and places that can take your mind off things
crisis.planPeople: People you can ask for help
crisis.planSafeEnvironment: Ways to make your surroundings safer
crisis.trustedTitle: Reach out to someone you trust
crisis.trustedBody: You don't have to explain everything. A simple sentence is enough, for example:
crisis.trustedExample1: I'm not doing okay. Can we talk for a bit?
crisis.trustedExample2: Could you stay with me for a while? I don't want to be alone right now.
crisis.acknowledge: I have read the information on this page.
crisis.continueHint: The continue button becomes available after you tick the box above.

results.title: Your screening results

radar.title: Emotional balance
radar.label: Radar chart of DASS-21 scores: depression {depression}, anxiety {anxiety}, stress {stress}, each out of 42.

results.priorityTitle: We recommend talking to a professional
results.priorityBody: Your results show extremely severe symptoms. Talking to a professional can really help with this. You can bring a report of these results to a psychologist, your campus counselling service, or a public health centre.
results.supportBody: If you need someone to talk to, you can contact the services below.
results.disclaimer: These results come from a self-screening (DASS-21), not a diagnosis. Only a professional, such as a psychologist or psychiatrist, can fully assess how you are doing.
results.downloadReport: Prepare a report for a psychologist
results.reportStep: Choose the report language and contents, then download a PDF to bring to a consultation.
results.tipsStep: Sign in or create an account to view evidence-based tips and save your progress.
results.deviceBody: These results are only saved in this device's browser. Delete them if you share this device.
results.clearDeviceQuestion: Delete all answers and results from this device?
results.instrumentNote: Scoring uses the DASS-21 (Lovibond & Lovibond, 1995): the 7 items of each dimension are summed and doubled, then compared with the official category cutoffs.

report.title: Report for a psychologist
report.intro: This two-page PDF summarises your screening so a psychologist can read it quickly: scores, answers by item, details about the instrument, and support services. If you write notes for your psychologist, they become a third page.
report.privacy: The report is created on your device. Nothing is sent to a server, and the file name does not include your name.
report.nicknameHint: Printed on the report. Leave it empty if you prefer.
report.includeSafetyHint: It shows your answer to the safety question and whether the crisis screen was shown. This helps a psychologist understand how you are doing more quickly, but you can leave it out.
report.previewNote: Page 2 lists your answers by item, details about the instrument, and support services for {country}.
report.error: The report could not be created. Please try again.

pdf.reportCodeNote: a random code, not an identity
pdf.safetyNote: This question is separate from the DASS-21 and is not part of the score.
pdf.disclaimer: This is a self-screening result from the DASS-21, not a diagnosis. It needs to be reviewed by a professional, such as a psychologist or psychiatrist.
pdf.englishItemsNote: Item text is shown in English (the official version) because the Indonesian text is not available yet.
pdf.scoringValue: The 7 items of each dimension are summed and doubled (range 0–42), then compared with the category cutoffs below.
pdf.footer: Made with Solace on {date}. A screening, not a diagnosis.
pdf.notesByUser: Written by the user in their own words.
pdf.notesByAi: Tidied with AI from the user's own writing and checked by the user before download. Not professional advice.

report.languageHint: Choose the language your psychologist reads most easily. This does not change the language of Solace.

notes.title: Notes for your psychologist (optional)
notes.intro: Answer in your own words, and skip any question you prefer not to answer. The notes only live on this page while it is open and are printed on page 3 of the report.

questions.since: Since when have you felt this way?
questions.hardest: What troubles you most in your daily life?
questions.ask: What would you like to ask the psychologist?
questions.hope: What do you hope for from the first session?

notes.include: Include the notes in the report
notes.includeHint: The notes are printed on page 3, so the psychologist can understand your story sooner.
notes.previewIncluded: Notes for your psychologist are included on page 3.

ai.hint: The AI only tidies your own words. It does not judge, diagnose, or add advice.
ai.signIn: Sign in to your account to tidy your notes with AI. Notes on this page are not saved, so sign in before you start writing.
ai.consentSent: What is sent: only the text you typed in these five boxes.
ai.consentNotSent: What is not sent: your screening answers, scores, username, and account data.
ai.consentProvider: Recipient: OpenRouter, which passes it to the model {model}.
ai.consentFallback: If that model is unavailable (busy, down, or too slow), the same request is passed once to the backup model {model}, with the same privacy settings.
ai.consentRetention: Requests are sent with settings that only allow providers that do not keep your data or use it to train models.
ai.consentLabel: The result is made by AI and is not professional advice. You can still edit it before downloading.
ai.done: Tidied by AI from your words; not professional advice. Check and edit before downloading.
ai.revert: Go back to my own text
ai.limited: You have reached today's AI limit. Your notes can still be downloaded as they are.
ai.busy: The AI provider is limiting requests right now. Try again later. Your notes can still be downloaded as they are.
ai.error: The AI is not available right now. Your notes can still be downloaded as they are.
ai.empty: Write at least one answer first.

explanation.introNormal: Your result for {subscale} is in the normal range.
explanation.depression: This dimension looks at things like low mood, losing interest or drive, and feeling that life has little meaning over the past week.
explanation.anxiety: This dimension looks at things like your body's reactions to anxiety (such as breathing or heartbeat), feelings of panic, and feeling scared without a clear reason over the past week.
explanation.stress: This dimension looks at things like finding it hard to relax, feeling tense or restless, and getting irritated easily over the past week.

advice.normal: Keep looking after the things that help you feel well.
advice.mild: Notice how your feelings change over the next few weeks, and give yourself room to rest.
advice.moderate: It may help to pay closer attention to this; talking to someone you trust or to a professional can help.
advice.severe: Talking to a professional can really help with this.
advice.extremely_severe: We recommend talking to a professional; you don't have to face this alone.

directory.countryHint: Choose the country you are in. This is separate from the language setting.

comingSoon.tipsBody: We are preparing the tips plan and the email-free account, and they will be available on this page soon.

notFound.title: Page not found
notFound.body: The page you are looking for does not exist or has moved.

account.title: Your Solace account
account.homeIntro: An account keeps your screening history, safety plan, check-ins, and chosen tips. Everything is encrypted in your browser before it is sent, so the Solace server only stores data it cannot read.
account.noEmail: No email, real name, or student ID. Just a username and a passphrase.
account.recover: Recover access with your recovery kit
account.unavailableBody: Screening, results, the PDF report, and the safety plan all work without an account. Accounts with end-to-end encryption will open here once their storage is ready.
account.requiredBody: Personal tips and your history are kept in your account, encrypted in your browser. Sign in or create an account without an email to continue.
account.usernameHint: 3–32 characters: lower-case letters, numbers, dots, dashes, or underscores. Better not your real name or student ID.
account.usernameInvalid: A username needs 3–32 characters: lower-case letters, numbers, dots, dashes, or underscores, and cannot be an email address.
account.passphraseHint: At least 12 characters. A few random words are easier to remember and stronger than one complicated word.
account.passphraseMismatch: The two passphrases do not match yet.
account.weakPassphrase: This passphrase is too easy to guess. Try combining a few unrelated words.
account.consequenceBody: Solace cannot read or reset your passphrase. If you forget your passphrase and also lose your recovery kit, nobody can recover your data, not even us.
account.consequenceAgree: I understand and will keep my recovery kit somewhere safe.
account.creating: Securing your data… this takes a few seconds.
account.kitBody: This code is the only way back in if you forget your passphrase. It is shown only once, so download or copy it now.
account.kitSaved: I have saved my recovery kit somewhere safe.
account.imported: Your last screening result on this device has been saved to your account.
account.recoverIntro: Enter your username, the code from your recovery kit, and a new passphrase. All your data stays as it is.
account.recoverCodeHint: 52 characters. Case, spaces, and dashes do not matter.
account.signInIntro: Your passphrase is never sent to the server; your browser uses it to open your data.
account.signUpIntro: Your account is created and encrypted in your browser. Afterwards, you will receive a recovery kit.

error.accounts_disabled: Accounts are not available right now.

account.homeSignedIn: Your data is open on this device until you sign out, or automatically after 30 minutes without activity.
account.linkHistoryDescription: Revisit your results and changes over time.
account.linkTipsDescription: Explore small next steps and exercises to try.
account.linkPlanDescription: Keep the support steps you want to remember.
account.changed: Your passphrase has been changed. Your recovery kit still works.
account.exportBody: Download everything in your account as decrypted JSON. The file is made in your browser.
account.deleteBody: Your account, history, safety plan, check-ins, and tip notes will be permanently deleted from the server. This cannot be undone.

tips.title: Tips for you
tips.intro: Put together from your latest screening ({date}). These can help some people, and each one can be tried today in 10 minutes or less.
tips.noResultBody: Tips are put together from a screening result. Finish a screening first, then come back here.
tips.companion: These tips are a companion to professional care, not a replacement for it.
tips.wellbeingBody: Your results are in the normal range for all three dimensions. These three habits can help you keep feeling well.
tips.rescreen: Try screening again in 2–4 weeks to see how you are doing.
tips.professionalTitle: When and where to get professional help
tips.professionalBody: If these symptoms get in the way of your studies, work, sleep, or relationships, or they feel heavier over time, talking to a professional can really help. You do not have to wait until things get worse.
tips.placePuskesmas: Your nearest community health centre (Puskesmas): ask about mental health services or a psychologist.
tips.placeCampus: Your campus counselling or psychology service.
tips.placePsychologist: A licensed clinical psychologist or psychiatrist.
tips.professionalReport: Take a report to a psychologist
tips.professionalUrgent: If you do not feel safe right now, open the help screen.

evidenceLevel.guideline: Based on: WHO or NICE guidance

tips.progressError: Your tip notes were not saved. Please try again.
tips.notHelpfulBody: That's okay: not every approach suits everyone. You can swap it for another tip that is also backed by evidence.
tips.noAlternative: Solace has no other tip for this section yet. An exercise from the toolkit below, or talking to a professional, can be a next step.
tips.replacedBody: You can bring them back at any time.

ai.hint: Say how things are, if you like. The AI will respond in one or two sentences, then choose another tip from Solace's library, or just listen if that is what you need. The tip's content, steps, and sources stay exactly as written in the library.
ai.modeLegend: What do you need right now?
ai.modeListen: I just want to be heard
ai.contextLabel: Describe your situation in one sentence (optional)
ai.contextPlaceholder: For example: writing my thesis and sleeping badly
ai.contextLabelListen: Write what you are feeling or going through, in one sentence
ai.consentSent: Sent: the sentence you write here (if any) and, if you ask for a tip, the text of tips from Solace's library.
ai.consentNotSent: Not sent: your screening answers, scores, categories, username, or account data.
ai.consentProvider: Recipient: OpenRouter, which passes it to the {model} model.
ai.consentFallback: If that model is unavailable (busy, down, or too slow), the same request is passed once to the backup model {model}, with the same privacy settings.
ai.consentRetention: The request asks to be handled only by providers that do not keep your data or use it to train models.
ai.consentLabel: If you write a sentence, the AI responds to it in one or two sentences. That response is written by AI, not professional advice. The AI only selects a tip ID; tip content stays from Solace's library.
ai.resultLabel: Selected by AI; content unchanged from Solace's library, not professional advice.
ai.fallbackLabel: An automatic choice in Solace's library order, not an AI result. You can use it or close it.
ai.reflectionLabel: The AI's response to your sentence, not professional advice
ai.heardSupport: If this feels heavy or does not ease, talking to someone you trust or to a professional can really help. The "I need help now" button is always at the top of the page.
ai.limited: You have reached today's AI limit. "Try another tip" still works.
ai.busy: The AI provider is limiting requests right now. Try again later, or use "Try another tip".
ai.error: The AI is not available right now. "Try another tip" still works.
ai.listenUnavailable: The AI cannot respond right now. Thank you for writing it down; what you feel still matters.

tips.toolkitIntro: Short exercises you can use at any time.
tips.pmrIntro: Tense one group of muscles for about 5 seconds, then let go and notice the difference for 10 seconds. Skip any part of your body that is sore or injured.
tips.pmrStep2: Upper arms: bend your elbows and tighten your arms.
tips.pmrStep3: Shoulders: lift your shoulders towards your ears.
tips.pmrStep4: Face: frown and close your eyes tightly.
tips.pmrStep5: Chest and back: draw your shoulders back a little.
tips.pmrStep7: Legs: straighten your legs and press your heels into the floor.
tips.pmrRelease: Let go and notice the difference ({seconds} seconds)
tips.pmrDone: Done. Take a slow breath and notice your body.

plan.title: Safety plan
plan.intro: A safety plan is a personal note to help you get through hard moments. Fill in as much as you like; there are no right or wrong answers, and you can change it at any time.

hint.warningSigns: Thoughts, feelings, or situations that usually come before a hard moment. For example: not sleeping for a few days, starting to avoid friends.
hint.coping: Things you can do on your own to calm down. For example: slow breathing, a warm shower, listening to a particular song.
hint.distraction: People or places that can take your mind off things for a while. For example: chatting with a friend, going to the library or a park.
hint.people: People you can contact and ask for help. Write their names and how to reach them.
hint.professionals: Professional services you can contact, for example your campus counselling service or a service in Solace's help directory.
hint.safeEnvironment: Steps to make your surroundings safer in a hard moment, for example asking someone to stay with you or to keep things that could hurt you for a while.

plan.localOnly: You are not signed in, so this plan is not stored anywhere. Download the PDF before you close this page.
plan.localSignIn: Sign in to save it encrypted
plan.savedInAccount: Your plan is saved encrypted in your account. Only you can open it.
plan.saveError: Your plan was not saved. Please try again.
plan.downloadError: The PDF could not be made. Please try again.

pdf.intro: A personal plan to help get through hard moments. Keep it somewhere easy to reach.
pdf.disclaimer: Solace is a screening tool, not an emergency service. If you are in immediate danger, call an emergency number above.

history.tableHint: Scroll the table to see every score and report button. With a keyboard, use the arrow keys while the table is focused.

history.intro: Every screening saved in your account. The charts use the ×2 score (0–42) with the categories as background bands.
history.emptyBody: Finish a screening while signed in, and the result will appear here.
history.reminderTitle: It has been {days} days since your last screening
history.reminderBody: Screening again can help you see how things are going.
history.worseTitle: A category has risen to severe
history.worseBody: Compared with your previous screening, symptoms of {subscales} have risen to a severe level or higher. Talking to a professional can really help; you can take your latest screening report with you.
history.trendUp: The {subscale} category went up from {from} to {to}.
history.trendDown: The {subscale} category went down from {from} to {to}.
history.trendOnlyOne: Trends appear once you have two or more screenings.
history.chartBands: Background bands show the categories: normal, mild, moderate, severe, extremely severe.
history.downloadError: The report could not be made. Please try again.
history.checkinBody: How are you feeling today? This is not a score; it is a note for yourself.

history.notePlaceholder: For example: I feel anxious about tomorrow's presentation.
history.checkinError: The check-in was not saved. Please try again.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Solace lets you check on your mental health without handing over who you are. This page explains what is stored, where, and who can see it.
privacy.summary1: Solace never asks for an email address, real name, phone number, or student number.
privacy.summary2: A screening without an account never leaves your device.
privacy.summary3: Your account content is encrypted in your browser before it is sent. The server only stores an encrypted copy that we cannot read.
privacy.summary4: No ads, pixels, or tracking analytics.
privacy.deviceTitle: Without an account: data on your device
privacy.device1: Your screening answers, results, and the country chosen for the help directory are kept in this browser's storage (localStorage), so you can continue a screening.
privacy.device2: A screening draft that is not continued is deleted automatically after 7 days.
privacy.device3: Your language choice is kept in the NEXT_LOCALE cookie, and your theme choice in browser storage. Neither holds anything about you.
privacy.device4: Anyone using the same device can see your results. Use "Delete from this device" on the results page to delete them.
privacy.device5: The PDF report and the safety plan without an account are made in your browser; nothing is sent to the server.
privacy.accountTitle: With an account: what the server sees
privacy.account1: The username you chose. It is best not to use your real name or student number.
privacy.account2: Not your passphrase. Your browser only sends a derived key to sign in, and the server stores that as a hash.
privacy.account3: Not your answers, scores, categories, tips, safety plan, or check-ins. These are encrypted with a key that never leaves your browser, so the server only receives ciphertext.
privacy.account4: When data was created and changed, and its size. This metadata cannot be avoided.
privacy.account5: Signing in uses one cookie, solace_session, which page scripts cannot read and which is only sent to Solace. The session ends after 30 minutes without activity.
privacy.ip1: Your IP address is used briefly to limit excessive sign-in and sign-up attempts. It is kept in server memory, not in Solace's database.
privacy.ip2: The hosting provider (Vercel) may record IP addresses in its logs for a short time, under its own privacy policy.
privacy.metrics1: Solace counts five events per day: screening started, results viewed, report opened, tips opened, and account created.
privacy.metrics2: These are only daily totals, with no user ID, IP address, or cookie, stored on Solace's own server.
privacy.metrics3: Nothing is counted because you opened the crisis help screen.
privacy.crisis1: The crisis help screen is decided in your browser. No data is sent to the server or to anyone because you are in a crisis.
privacy.crisis2: Solace never contacts any person or organisation on your behalf.
privacy.ai1: The AI features are off until you read and accept their consent screen.
privacy.ai2: Only the text you write for that feature is sent, and for "Choose with AI" also the text of tips from Solace's library. Your screening answers, scores, categories, username, and account data are never sent.
privacy.ai3: Your text is checked in your browser first. If it contains words that suggest risk, the help screen opens and the AI is not called.
privacy.ai4: Requests go through OpenRouter, set to be handled only by providers that keep no data (zero data retention).
privacy.providers1: Vercel runs Solace's website and server, in the United States.
privacy.providers2: Neon stores the account database (usernames, times, and ciphertext), also in the United States.
privacy.providers3: OpenRouter only receives data if you use an AI feature.
privacy.providers4: Fonts are served from Solace's own server, and your browser is only allowed to connect to Solace. No clinic, hospital, or psychologist receives your data.
privacy.rights1: On the account page you can download everything in your account as a decrypted JSON file.
privacy.rights2: You can change your passphrase at any time; your data stays readable.
privacy.rights3: You can delete your account by typing your username. All account data is permanently deleted from the database. The database provider keeps a change history for at most 6 hours for emergency restores; after that the data is gone, and during that time it is only ciphertext.
privacy.rights4: If you forget your passphrase and lose your recovery kit, nobody can recover your data, including us.
privacy.law1: Solace is designed to follow the principles of data minimisation, consent, and the right to deletion in Indonesia's Personal Data Protection Law (UU No. 27 of 2022). Solace does not claim any compliance certification.
privacy.law2: Solace is meant for people aged 18 and over.
privacy.contact1: Questions or privacy problems can be raised through Solace's repository on GitHub.
